# Sound A/B review

Each GregGuns sound compared with the Techguns sound it replaces, generated by [`tools/audio-describe`](../../../tools/audio-describe/README.md) `compare`.

> [!NOTE]
> Claude can't take audio input. Each comparison reads both sounds' spectrograms, waveforms and measurements, plus listening notes from Qwen2-Audio, which did hear both files. Scores run 0-10 for how well the replacement fills the original's role and feel.

Reviewed 278 sounds: **59 rework**, **166 tweak**, **53 keep**. Mean score 5.9.

### sounds/npcs/turret_beep-06.ogg

Replaces `sounds/npcs/turret_beep-06.ogg`. **rework**, score 1/10, confidence high.

B is a 0.26 s block of continuous broadband noise with two sustained sine lines at ~5 kHz and ~3 kHz, while A is a 0.07 s stepped three-tone chirp followed by near silence. B misses the role entirely and sounds like a power-tool hiss rather than a turret beep.

| Aspect | Techguns (A) | GregGuns (B) | Severity |
|---|---|---|---|
| noise vs tone | Clean, tonal chirp (flatness ~0) made of discrete sine/square steps with only a faint broadband splash at the start. | Dominated by dense broadband noise (flatness 0.62) filling 20 Hz to 20 kHz at roughly -40 to -50 dB for the whole clip. | major |
| length/timing | Active chirp lasts only ~0.07 s (-40 dB by 0.06 s), then ~0.24 s of near silence. Active fraction 0.23. | Sustained for ~0.26 s with an abrupt cutoff and no decay. Active fraction 0.83. | major |
| envelope/decay | Short swell to peak at ~0.02 s, then a sharp drop of 40 dB. The shape is a quick blip that ends cleanly. | Flat, steady envelope (about -15 to -17 dB per tenth) with no shape, ending in a hard gate. | major |
| pitch | Stepped ascending pitch: ~1.5 kHz, ~3 kHz, then ~4.8 to 5.3 kHz in about 4 steps of 15-25 ms. | No pitch movement. Static lines at ~2.95 kHz and ~4.8-5.3 kHz persist across the whole clip, with no 1.5 kHz step and no stepping. | major |
| tonal balance | Centroid ~4.5 kHz, rolloff ~5.3 kHz, 20% mid and 80% presence, no air. | Centroid ~10 kHz, rolloff ~19 kHz, 48% air, 37% presence, only 14% mid. Far too hissy and bright. | major |
| loudness | Peak -9.5 dBFS, RMS -21.6 dB, short and punchy. | Peak -3.7 dBFS, RMS -16.9 dB, about 5 dB hotter RMS, and sustained so it feels much louder. | moderate |
| attack/transients | Clean tonal swell with a soft click at the start, distinct note onsets. | No discernible onset (attack reported at 0.16 s, onset count 0). It just starts as noise. | moderate |
| tail/reverb | Very faint ringing lines at 1.5k, 3k and 5k Hz at about -60 dB after the chirp, effectively inaudible. | No tail at all; hard cut at 0.26 s from full level. | minor |

**Missing:** Three-to-four step ascending chirp (1.5k, 3k, 4.8k, 5.3k Hz); Short 0.07 s blip with sharp cutoff; Silence/near-silence for the rest of the 0.31 s; Faint quiet ringing tail around -60 dB

**Extra:** Continuous full-band noise bed from 20 Hz to 20 kHz; Sustained static sine lines at ~3 kHz and ~5 kHz for 0.26 s; Heavy air-band hiss above 10 kHz

**Change notes:**
1. Remove the broadband noise bed completely. Keep at most a 3 ms, -30 dB noise click at 0 s, band-passed to 2-6 kHz.
2. Replace the sustained tones with 4 sequential blips: 1.5 kHz at 0-20 ms, 3.0 kHz at 20-40 ms, 4.8 kHz at 40-55 ms, 5.3 kHz at 55-70 ms. Use square or sine with a 3 ms fade-in and a 3-5 ms fade-out per step.
3. Give the whole chirp an envelope that swells to its peak at ~20 ms, holds, then drops 40 dB by ~70 ms. Gate hard after 70 ms.
4. Low-pass everything at ~8 kHz so the centroid sits near 4.5 kHz and air-band energy is under 1%.
5. Lower the peak to about -9.5 dBFS (reduce gain ~6 dB) and aim for RMS around -21 dB.
6. Add a very quiet tail: 1.5k, 3k and 5k sine ringing from 70 ms to 300 ms at -55 to -65 dB, decaying slowly. Pad with silence so the file totals 0.31 s.
7. Check the final spectrogram for lines that persist beyond 80 ms above -50 dB. Those are the clutter that should be removed.

### sounds/guns/revolver_reload_akimbo.ogg
